identity.title: The ALMA Frontier Fields Survey. III. 1.1 mm emission line identifications in Abell 2744, MACSJ 0416.1-2403, MACSJ 1149.5+2223, Abell 370, and Abell S1063

paper_type_evidence.quote: We perform a search for emission lines in the ALMA observations of five clusters which are part of the Frontier Fields and assess the reliability of our detection.

question.value: Can serendipitous emission lines be detected in the 1.1 mm continuum-oriented ALMA Frontier Fields mosaics of five lensing clusters, and are they reliable and identifiable with NIR counterparts?

evidence.quote: Our aim is to detect emission lines present in continuum oriented observations.
programs #2013.1.00999.S in cycle 2 and #2015.1.1425.S in cycle 3
The Local Oscillator frequency was set to 263.14 GHz ($\approx$1.1 mm), with two spectral windows (SPWs) placed in each sideband.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 SPWs, 1875 MHz each, 0.488 MHz channels, 7.45 GHz total; averaged to 7.813 MHz (~9 km/s)

evidence.quote: The correlator was set to Frequency Division Mode (FDM) with a bandwidth of 1875 MHz and a channel spacing of 0.488 MHz.
resulting in a final spectral resolution of 7.813 MHz ($\sim9{{\rm \thinspace km\thinspace s}^{-1}}$)

arrays.value: 12 m array, 126 pointings per field, ~4.6 arcmin^2 mosaics

evidence.quote: Each field was covered with 126 pointings to create mosaics spanning an area of $\approx4.6$ square arcminutes
These cubes have synthesized beam sizes of 0.63$''$$\times$0.49$''$ and position angle of 86.16$^\circ$ for A2744

sensitivity.value: ~0.8-1.0 (lower sideband) and ~0.9-1.3 (upper sideband) mJy/beam per 15.626 MHz channel

evidence.quote: we obtain sensitivity ranges of $\approx$0.8–1.0 and $\approx$0.9–1.3 mJy beam$^{-1}$ over a 15.626 MHz channel

provided.value: Deep NIR counterparts and photometry for line associations and photometric redshifts

evidence.quote: we expect that an emission line candidate co-spatial to a NIR detected galaxy should increase the probability of this candidate being real and thus use the NIR images for this purpose.

provided.value: Grism spectroscopic redshift for MACSJ0416-EL03 counterpart (z=1.849)

evidence.quote: The NIR galaxy has been detected as part of the Grism Lens-Amplified Survey from Space (cite: Treu2015) with a redshift of $z=1.849$.

what.value: H-alpha based SFRs and morphology classification for A370-EL01 and AS1063-EL01 hosts

evidence.quote: (cite: Vulcani2016) presented H$\alpha$ observations for several galaxies of the FFs
We estimate the magnification values as in (cite: Coe2015), by taking the 16th, 50th and 84th percentiles

what.value: 1.1 mm continuum source redshifts, e.g. A2744-ID02 z~2.482

evidence.quote: The redshift for A2744-ID02 is reported in (cite: Laporte2017) as $z\approx2.482$ for the brightest red clump.

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Simulated Gaussian-noise cubes (>100) convolved with the real synthesized beams, used to estimate false detection probability

evidence.quote: together with the $95\%$ confidence region assessed by simulating over 100 data cubes
We created data cubes of the observations using natural weighting, which provides the best sensitivity

smoothing.value: Cubes at 2, 4, 8, 16x native resolution (15.6-125 MHz); spectral Gaussian convolution sigma 2-48x native

evidence.quote: The $\sigma_{\rm convolution}$ values used for the Gaussian convolution range from 2 to 48 times the native resolution

what.value: Configuration, reduction and continuum imaging of cycle 2 data

evidence.quote: In GL17, we presented the configuration, reduction and continuum imaging of the cycle 2 observations.
Full details of the cycle 3 observations will be presented in (cite: Gonzalez-Lopez2017b).
We estimate the magnification values as in (cite: Coe2015)

unstated_but_needed: CASA version and calibration/imaging details (deferred to GL17)
Spectral line-search code/software not named or released
Exact S/N rms estimation scheme per channel
Cell size, image size, and masking for cubes
MAGPHYS SED fit settings and priors
Which lens models/versions per cluster in full

method.value: Natural-weighted dirty cubes per SPW binned to 2,4,8,16x native channels

evidence.quote: we generated four data cubes per SPW, each with a different spectral resolution.

method.value: Convolve spectrally with Gaussians, take per-channel rms, select cells S/N>=5

evidence.quote: we take the rms in each spectral channel and select those cells with $S/N\geq5$.
Therefore assuming a Gaussian shape for emission line search is justified.

method.value: Run same search on simulated Gaussian-noise cubes (PBC>=0.5 cells, convolved with real beam); P=N(>S/N)/N_total

evidence.quote: We define this probability as $P_{S/N}=N_{>S/N}/N_{total}$
This cut yields a total of 26 candidates

assumptions.value: Gaussian, spatially and spectrally independent noise

evidence.quote: We assume here that the noise in the ALMA-FFs data can be approximated by a Gaussian distribution

validation.value: Compared real vs simulated S/N distributions and with negative-image FDR

evidence.quote: A comparison between simulations and negative image FDR probabilities for each cluster is shown in Fig. [4]

method.value: Corrected-Poisson P_sep=1-exp(n pi sep^2); P=P_S/N x P_sep; reliable if P<=0.05 and P_S/N<=0.99

evidence.quote: We select as reliable emission line candidates those candidates with $P\leq0.05$ and $P_{S/N}\le0.99$.

validation.value: Second method with random simulated positions gave similar probabilities

evidence.quote: We confirmed that both estimators return similar probabilities

method.value: Gaussian fit to spectra at candidate centroids assuming point sources

evidence.quote: obtained from fitting a Gaussian function to the spectra extracted at the centroid positions of the line candidates, assuming point sources

validation.value: Compared with flux integrated from collapsed line map

evidence.quote: We can compare the flux estimated from assuming a point source with that obtained from integrating the collapsed line.

method.value: SED fitting of NIR photometry of nearest counterpart; match CO/CI/[NII]/[CII] lines to redshift

evidence.quote: We use the NIR photometry of the nearest counterpart to estimate the SFR by fitting the spectral energy distribution using the high-redshift MAGPHYS code

assumptions.value: Redshift of nearest counterpart applies to the line

evidence.quote: We make the implicit assumption here that the photometric or spectroscopic redshift of the nearest counterpart applies also to the emission line

validation.value: Compare predicted vs observed line flux; velocity shift vs optical redshift

evidence.quote: we further compared the observed line fluxes with those estimated from the observed SFRs and redshifts to weed out inconsistent identifications.

method.value: Percentiles of FF lens-model magnifications; M_H2 from CO luminosity with alpha_CO and CO excitation ratio; t_dep=M_H2/SFR

evidence.quote: We can then estimate the depletion timescales over which the star-formation would use up the available molecular gas, $t_{\rm dep}={\rm M}_{\rm H2}/{\rm SFR}$.
For CO(3-2), we use a value of $R_{31}\sim0.56$.

validation.value: Expected continuum from Scoville2016 compared with observed continuum

evidence.quote: For A2744-EL01, the expected continuum level is $\sim$0.4 mJy; this should have been detected in the $S/N\geq5$ analysis presented in GL17.

used_for.value: SED fitting for photometric redshift and SFR

evidence.quote: fitting the spectral energy distribution using the high-redshift MAGPHYS code

results_numeric.quantity: Number of line candidates with P_S/N<=0.99

evidence.quote: This cut yields a total of 26 candidates
Among these, we find nine candidates with $P\leq0.05$
${\rm M}_{\rm H2}=(2.4\pm0.4)\times10^{10}\times\left(\frac{\alpha_{\rm CO}}{0.8}\right)
we find depletion times of $t_{\rm dep}\sim0.9$ Gyr and $t_{\rm dep}\sim0.07$ Gyr, respectively.

evidence.loc: Comparison with blind line scan surveys
evidence.quote: we obtain a detection rate of $0.05^{+0.02}_{-0.02}$ GHz$^{-1}$ square arcmin$^{-1}$ in the ALMA-FFs

findings_qualitative.value: AS1063-EL01 host is a jellyfish galaxy with CO offset consistent with ram-pressure stripping direction

evidence.quote: The host galaxy of AS1063-EL01 is classified as a so-called ’jellyfish’ galaxy with signs of ram pressure stripping

claims.hypothesis: Serendipitous lines can be found and identified in continuum-oriented mosaics with deep NIR data
claims.experiment: Line search in five FF cubes, MC false-detection probabilities, NIR association
claims.result: 26 candidates, 9 reliable, 6 with secure/tentative CO identifications
claims.finding: Feasible but yields few high-significance lines compared to blind scans

evidence.quote: The low number of high-significance line detections, however, confirms that such surveys are not as optimal as blind line scans.

claims.hypothesis: Negative-image FDR is unreliable versus Monte Carlo
claims.result: Negative image gives noisier, sharper probabilities
claims.finding: Monte Carlo simulations should be used

evidence.quote: returns a much noisier and sharper probability distribution for all of the clusters

claims.experiment: M_H2 and depletion times from CO
claims.finding: MACSJ0416-EL03 and AS1063-EL01 starburst-like; others main-sequence-like (alpha_CO dependent)

evidence.quote: We can then estimate the depletion timescales over which the star-formation would use up the available molecular gas

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Negative-image FDR rejected in favor of Monte Carlo

evidence.quote: We propose that Monte Carlo simulations can yield a more realistic understanding

limitations_admitted.value: Many candidates are narrow (FWHM<50 km/s) and may be noise; narrow frequency coverage limits secure identifications

evidence.quote: we acknowledge that the narrow emission line candidates selected have a higher probability of being false

referee_caveats_inferred: Line identifications depend on assumed counterpart redshift and single lines
Molecular masses depend strongly on alpha_CO and excitation assumed
Gaussian-noise assumption tested only on MACSJ0416

missing_for_reproduction: Calibrated cubes and CASA settings deferred to GL17
Counterpart catalogs and SED setup not given
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Large: five 126-pointing band 6 mosaics, likely hundreds of GB to ~1 TB raw
reproducibility.score_reason: Clear search and probability recipe, but search code, cube parameters and calibration are not specified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Recipe incomplete (no code, imaging details deferred to other papers) and depends on external catalogs.

methods_papers.why: ALMA-FF cycle 2 configuration, reduction and imaging

companion_papers.why: cycle 3 observations and low-significance continuum sources
